status_summary: Recruiter access and Junior ROTC are addressed in law; the ASVAB requirement is not. S. 3052 (introduced 2025-10-23) would have required schools to give military recruiters the same campus access as other prospective employers, at least four recruitment events a year on request, and student contact information. Public Law 119-60, the FY2026 NDAA enacted 2025-12-18, contains Sec. 531, which requires recruiter access equivalent to that of employers and colleges, at least one in-person event a year on request, and student contact data within 30 days, and Sec. 542, which raises the required Junior ROTC unit range from 3,400 to 4,000 to 3,600 to 4,200 effective 2027-10-01. A Senate committee chairman's release of 2026-05-05 says DOD directed an increase in Junior ROTC programs and delegated authority to set unit numbers to the Under Secretary for Personnel and Readiness, and CRS counted 3,475 units in FY2025. Neither section mentions the ASVAB, and no requirement that all students in federally funded schools take it was found.

timeline.event: S. 3052 introduced to require schools to give military recruiters the same campus access as other prospective employers, at least four in-person recruitment events a year on request, and student contact information.

President signs the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60). Sec. 531 requires local educational agencies to give military recruiters access equivalent to that given to employers and colleges, at least one in-person recruitment event per academic year on request, and student contact information within 30 days of a request; Sec. 542 raises the Junior ROTC unit range from 3,400 to 4,000 to 3,600 to 4,200, effective 2027-10-01.
Sponsors' press release says the recruiter access bill was signed into law as part of the FY2026 NDAA.

Senate Armed Services chairman states DOD directed an increase in JROTC programs, the Secretary of Defense delegated authority to set unit numbers to the Under Secretary for Personnel and Readiness, and the FY2027 request renews JROTC funding.

title: Expand recruiter access to schools, universal ASVAB and Junior ROTC units
uncertainties: The text of Sec. 531 and Sec. 542 of Public Law 119-60 was read through a browser retrieval supplied to the project; direct fetches by the research tools and by the independent reviewer returned only the table of contents, so the section terms rest on that retrieval; the retrieval also reports that neither section mentions the ASVAB. Sec. 531 differs from S. 3052 as introduced on the number of required events (one per year against four), and the enacted section's own effective date was not reported. Sec. 542 changes the range that existed before the review period (3,400 to 4,000) to 3,600 to 4,200 effective 2027-10-01, so that increase was enacted within the review period but is not yet operative; the retrieval also says Sec. 542 repeals Sec. 545 of the FY2025 NDAA, which may be the source of the 3,500 to 4,100 range from 2026-10-01 that CRS describes (inference). The Wicker release gives no unit numbers or section. Sec. 534, on Armed Forces Qualification Test scores for a preparatory course, is not an ASVAB requirement for students and was not treated as one.
